# CRAY — finite-moment information about a quantum environment

Research record: 13 October 2026.

## Status

This continuation derives two related environmental-information results. The first gives exact extremal **ground impurity energies** among quadratic fermionic baths with specified signed-band coupling weights and first absolute-energy moments. The second, for spectrally symmetric quadratic baths, uses coupling weights and **squared-energy moments** to obtain an interaction-uniform uncertainty certificate computable entirely from one-particle matrices. The moment contracts are different and must not be interchanged.

The mathematical arguments are given below. They have not been independently refereed or formalized. Historical novelty of these particular combinations and characterizations has not been established. Variational compression, self-adjoint dilation, moment inequalities, hybridization representations, and causal Green functions are established ingredients, not inventions of this investigation.

The implementation includes numerical interacting checks, an independently specified finite-range metallic-reservoir control, an exact rational uncertainty certificate, a sampling-cost experiment, and an exact counterexample to extending single-particle spectral sufficiency to an interacting bath. No real molecule or adsorption-site energy has been calculated. No runtime advantage over a specialized impurity solver has been demonstrated. This is a substantive mathematical continuation, not a completed transformative chemical-design capability.

## 1. Scientific task and current comparison

The target considered was a certified local adsorption/design energy difference in a metallic environment, with CO atop versus hollow adsorption on Cu(111) as a documented motivating task. It is not an untouched benchmark. The current FEMION paper, revised 9 April 2026, treats CO/Cu(111) and hydrogen desorption using local AFQMC with a global RPA treatment of nonlocal screening [1]. Its inclusion of nonlocal correlation is important: replacing the whole substrate by an exactly quadratic bath is not automatically an equivalent physical model.

# Shared-bath design contrasts: exact obstruction and a thermal refinement

Integration-derived mathematics, 2026-10-13. Capital pin

These are restricted internal deductions, not external correctness or priority
clearance. The source's finite-bath moment and causal Green arguments are the
explicit dependencies. Standard variational, Gibbs, CAR, Pinsker and Duhamel
tools are credited rather than claimed as new primitives.

## 1. Contract

Use the source's finite quadratic fermionic bath and grand-canonical impurity
energy/potential. Both designs have the **same impurity modes, coupling and bare
bath**, and differ only in their supplied even number-conserving impurity
Hamiltonians `H_A,0,H_A,1`. Write `Delta(Gamma)=F_1(Gamma)-F_0(Gamma)` at fixed
inverse temperature beta; the bare bath subtraction cancels. The zero-temperature
version uses the bath-subtracted ground energies. The bath spectral measure is
symmetric, and its acquired squared-energy moments give physical envelopes
`Gamma_l<=Gamma<=Gamma_h` in the source's Loewner sense. No canonical sector,
interacting-substrate reduction or physical spectral acquisition is inferred.

## 2. Individually extremal baths need not extremize the contrast

Take two uncoupled impurity channels, one absolute-energy band `[0,1]`, and
matrix moment data

    W=I_2, S=I_2/4.

In each channel the lower hybridization/upper-energy bath L has poles `+/-1/2`
with pair-total weight one. The upper hybridization/lower-energy bath H has a
zero pole of weight `3/4` and poles `+/-1` with pair-total weight `1/4`. Thus the
single-channel measures in `s=epsilon^2` are

    nu_L=delta_(1/4),
    nu_H=(3/4)delta_0+(1/4)delta_1.

Both have mass one and first s-moment `1/4`. The common-bath information class
also permits L in one channel and H in the other. This mixed bath does not
change the matrix moments, which remain exactly the displayed scalar matrices.

Choose designs

    H_A,0=10 n_1,  H_A,1=10 n_0.

Both all-L and all-H baths give `Delta=0`, since interchanging channels maps
the two full Hamiltonians unitarily. Denote by `e_x(B)` the normalized
single-channel ground impurity energy at impurity level x with bath B. For the
mixed bath `(H,L)`, the exact contrast is

    Delta(H,L)=e_10(H)+e_0(L)-e_0(H)-e_10(L)=R_0-R_10,
    R_x=e_x(L)-e_x(H)>=0.
